# Merchant Financial Advisory LLC (MFA)

> Accounting, bookkeeping, tax preparation and advisory firm in Princeton, New Jersey. Serves small and mid-sized businesses and individuals in New Jersey, New York City and nationwide, forms LLCs in all 50 states, and sells digital tax and bookkeeping tools. Founded by Zain Merchant, ACCA, formerly of PwC.

Contact: info@mfa-advisory.com, (347) 205-4468. Location: Princeton, New Jersey (no public street address; work is done remotely by video, phone and secure upload). Languages: English, Hindi, Urdu. Book a 30-minute consultation: https://mfa-advisory.com/#book. Replies to inquiries within one to three business days.

Not a law firm. MFA does not perform audits or issue audit, review or compilation reports. Content on the site is general information, not tax, legal or financial advice.

## Services and public prices
- [Services](https://mfa-advisory.com/services/): tax preparation, tax planning, bookkeeping, financial reporting, fractional CFO, audit support, technical accounting, business advisory
- [LLC formation in all 50 states](https://mfa-advisory.com/llc-formation/): $150 / $249 / $649 plus the state fee, paid once; state-by-state fees and rules
- [Bookkeeping cleanup and catch-up](https://mfa-advisory.com/bookkeeping-cleanup/): fixed quote request
- [Machine-readable catalog](https://mfa-advisory.com/catalog.json): all services, prices, tools and products as schema.org JSON

## Tools (online calculators and checkers)
- [Resources hub](https://mfa-advisory.com/resources/): all tools, calendars, templates and guides
- [1099 Contractor Tracker: Who Needs a 1099-NEC in 2026](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/1099-contractor-tracker/): Track vendors, W-9s and payments, see who needs a 1099-NEC at the 2026 $2,000 threshold, and export to CSV. Data stays in your browser.
- [1099 Tax Calculator 2026: Self-Employment, NJ & NY](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/1099-tax-calculator/): Estimate the self-employment tax, federal income tax and NJ or NY tax on your 1099 income, plus the share of every payment to set aside.
- [Break-Even Calculator for Small Businesses](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/break-even-calculator/): Find your break-even point in sales and units from monthly fixed costs, price and variable cost. For product and service businesses, with a profit goal.
- [Do I Need to Send a 1099? 2026 Payments Checker](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/do-i-need-to-send-a-1099/): Four questions show whether a 2026 payment needs a Form 1099-NEC or 1099-MISC: the $2,000 threshold, card and corporation exceptions, and deadlines.
- [Home Office Deduction Calculator 2026](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/home-office-deduction-calculator/): Compare the simplified ($5 per square foot, up to 300) and regular home office deduction methods for 2026 side by side.
- [Is It Tax Deductible? 2026 Business Write-Off Finder](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/): Can I write it off? Search 58 business expense deductions for 2026: what self-employed people can deduct, the limits, records and IRS source.
- [Mileage Deduction Calculator 2026 (IRS Standard Rates)](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/mileage-deduction-calculator/): Calculate your 2026 business mileage deduction with the IRS standard rates, including the split between the January to June and July to December rates.
- [Paycheck Tax Calculator 2026 (Federal, FICA, NJ & NY)](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/paycheck-tax-calculator/): Estimate W-2 take-home pay per paycheck after federal income tax, Social Security, Medicare and New Jersey or New York tax.
- [Profit Margin & Markup Calculator](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/profit-margin-calculator/): Calculate gross profit margin and markup from cost and price, or the selling price for a target margin or markup. Includes a margin vs. markup guide.
- [Quarterly Estimated Tax Calculator 2026: Fed, NJ & NY](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/quarterly-estimated-tax-calculator/): Estimate your four 2026 quarterly tax payments: self-employment tax, federal income tax and NJ or NY tax, with due dates and the safe-harbor amount.
- [S Corp Tax Savings Calculator: Is an S Corp Worth It?](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/s-corp-tax-savings-calculator/): Compare self-employment tax as an LLC with payroll taxes as an S corporation. See annual savings after costs and the break-even profit.
- [2027 Business Tax Deadlines by Entity: Fed, NJ & NY](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/tax-deadlines-2027/): Every 2027 federal, New Jersey and New York tax deadline for sole proprietors, partnerships, S and C corporations, employers and nonprofits.
- [W-9 Request Email Templates for Vendors](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/w-9-request-email-template/): Copy-ready W-9 request emails for new vendors, year-end 1099 prep and reminders. Personalize the names and deadline, then copy with one click.

## Is It Deductible? (2026 business expense deductions, one line per expense)
- [Is it tax deductible? 2026 business write-off finder](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/): search 58 common business expenses; verdict, rule, limits, records to keep and the IRS source for each
- [Dataset (JSON)](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/deductions.json): the same entries as structured data. Cite with a link to the page.
- [Home office](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#home-office): It depends. You can deduct part of your home costs if a specific area is used regularly and exclusively for your business and is your principal place of business (or where you meet clients).
- [Office rent](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#office-rent): 100% deductible. Rent you pay for office, retail or other business space is deductible in the year it applies to.
- [Coworking space or shared desk](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#coworking): 100% deductible. A coworking membership, desk rental or meeting-room booking used for your business is rent for business space and is deductible.
- [Utilities (electric, gas, water)](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#utilities): It depends. Utilities for a business location (an office, shop or studio) are deductible.
- [Office supplies and postage](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#office-supplies): 100% deductible. Office supplies and postage used in your business are deductible.
- [Work clothes and uniforms](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#uniforms): It depends. Clothing is deductible only if your work requires it and it isn't suitable for ordinary street wear, such as protective gear or a uniform you wouldn't wear outside work.
- [Car mileage (standard rate)](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#mileage): Partly deductible. Deduct your business miles times the IRS standard mileage rate instead of tracking actual car costs.
- [Car expenses (actual costs)](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#vehicle-actual-expenses): Partly deductible. Instead of the standard rate, you can deduct the business share of what the car actually costs: gas, oil, repairs, tires, insurance, registration, licenses and depreciation or lease payments.
- [Parking and tolls](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#parking-tolls): 100% deductible. Parking fees and tolls for business trips are deductible on top of either the standard mileage rate or actual expenses.
- [Business travel (flights, hotels)](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#business-travel): Deductible. Ordinary and necessary costs of traveling away from your tax home overnight for business are deductible: transportation, lodging, taxis or rideshare at the destination, baggage, laundry and business calls.
- [Meals while traveling](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#travel-meals): 50% deductible. Meals while you're traveling away from home on business are generally 50% deductible.
- [Business meals](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#meals): 50% deductible. A meal with a client, customer or business contact is generally 50% deductible if it isn't lavish, you (or an employee) are there, and it has a business purpose.
- [Entertainment (tickets, golf, shows)](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#entertainment): Not deductible. Entertainment is not deductible, even with a clear business purpose.
- [Staff parties and team events](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#employee-parties): 100% deductible. Recreational and social events mainly for your employees, such as a holiday party or summer picnic, are an exception to the entertainment and 50% meal limits.
- [Snacks and meals for employees at work](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#employee-meals): Not deductible. Starting in 2026, an employer can no longer deduct the cost of food and drinks provided to employees through an on-site eating facility, as de minimis fringe benefits, or for the employer's convenience.
- [Cell phone and phone service](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#cell-phone): Partly deductible. The business share of your cell phone plan is deductible.
- [Internet service](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#internet): Partly deductible. Internet service for a business location is deductible.
- [Software and subscriptions](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#software-subscriptions): Deductible. Monthly or annual subscriptions to software and online services you use for your business are ordinary business expenses.
- [Laptop or computer](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#computer): It depends. A computer used in your business is a business asset.
- [Equipment and machinery (Section 179)](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#section-179): Deductible. Section 179 lets you deduct the cost of qualifying business equipment, furniture and off-the-shelf software in the year you start using it, instead of depreciating it over several years.
- [Bonus depreciation](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#bonus-depreciation): 100% deductible. Qualified property acquired and placed in service after Jan.
- [Small equipment purchases ($2,500 or less)](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#de-minimis-safe-harbor): Deductible. With the de minimis safe harbor election you can deduct, rather than depreciate, tangible items that cost $2,500 or less per invoice or item.
- [Tools and small equipment](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#tools-equipment): Deductible. Tools and professional instruments you normally use up within a year can be deducted when bought.
- [Repairs vs. improvements](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#repairs-vs-improvements): It depends. Incidental repairs and routine maintenance that keep property in normal working order are deductible.
- [Contractor and freelancer payments](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#contractors): 100% deductible. Payments to independent contractors for work done for your business are deductible as contract labor.
- [Employee wages](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#wages): 100% deductible. Reasonable wages, salaries and bonuses you pay employees for work actually done are deductible.
- [Employer payroll taxes](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#payroll-taxes): 100% deductible. The employer's share of Social Security and Medicare taxes, federal unemployment tax (FUTA) and state unemployment contributions are deductible business taxes.
- [Employee benefit programs](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#employee-benefits): Deductible. Contributions to employee benefit programs, such as accident and health plans, group-term life insurance and dependent care assistance, are deductible.
- [Employee awards and holiday gifts](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#achievement-awards): Deductible. Tangible awards for length of service or safety, given as part of a meaningful presentation, are deductible within limits.
- [Business insurance](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#business-insurance): 100% deductible. Premiums for business insurance, such as general or professional liability, property and workers' compensation coverage, are deductible.
- [Health insurance (self-employed)](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#self-employed-health-insurance): It depends. If you're self-employed with a profit, you can deduct medical, dental, vision and qualified long-term care premiums for yourself, your spouse and dependents (and a child under 27).
- [Life insurance premiums](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#life-insurance): Not deductible. You can't deduct premiums on a life insurance policy when you or your business is directly or indirectly a beneficiary.
- [SEP-IRA contributions](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#sep-ira): Deductible. Contributions to a SEP-IRA for yourself are deductible on Schedule 1, not Schedule C; contributions for employees go on Schedule C.
- [Solo 401(k) contributions](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#solo-401k): Deductible. In a one-participant 401(k) you can contribute as both employee (elective deferrals) and employer (profit-sharing).
- [Retirement contributions for employees](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#employee-retirement): Deductible. Contributions you make to a retirement plan for the benefit of your employees are deductible on Schedule C.
- [Legal and accounting fees](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#legal-professional-fees): 100% deductible. Fees for accountants, bookkeepers, attorneys and other professionals that are ordinary and necessary for your business are deductible.
- [Tax preparation fees](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#tax-prep-fees): Partly deductible. Tax preparation and tax advice fees related to your business are deductible on Schedule C.
- [Professional and trade association dues](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#professional-dues): Deductible. Dues to professional organizations, trade associations, business leagues, chambers of commerce, real estate boards and civic or public service groups are deductible, as long as the group's main purpose isn't entertainment.
- [Advertising and marketing](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#advertising): 100% deductible. Advertising and other selling expenses, such as online ads, print ads, business cards, flyers and promotional campaigns, are ordinary business expenses.
- [Gifts to clients](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#client-gifts): Partly deductible. Business gifts to clients, customers and referral partners are deductible, but only up to $25 per person per year.
- [Branded promotional items](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#promotional-items): Deductible. Low-cost items with your business name clearly and permanently imprinted, handed out widely (pens, keychains, desk sets and the like), don't count as gifts, so the $25 limit doesn't apply.
- [Courses, training and conferences](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#business-education): It depends. Education that maintains or improves skills you need in your current business, or is required by law to keep your status, is deductible.
- [Bank and card processing fees](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#bank-card-fees): 100% deductible. Monthly fees on a business bank account, wire fees and the fees payment processors take from your sales are ordinary and necessary business expenses.
- [Interest on business loans and credit cards](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#business-interest): Partly deductible. Interest on money borrowed for your business is deductible.
- [Unpaid invoices (bad debts)](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#bad-debts): It depends. A business bad debt is deductible only if the amount was already included in your income.
- [Startup costs](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#startup-costs): Partly deductible. Costs of investigating or setting up a business before it opens (market research, pre-opening advertising, training, consultants) can be deducted up to $5,000 in the year you start, with the rest amortized over 180 months.
- [Business formation costs](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#organizational-costs): Partly deductible. Costs to form a corporation or partnership (including a multi-member LLC), such as state filing fees and legal fees for the organizing documents, can be deducted up to $5,000 in the first year, with the rest amortized over 180 months.
- [Inventory and cost of goods sold](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#inventory-cogs): It depends. Products you buy or make to sell aren't deducted when bought.
- [Shipping and postage](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#shipping-postage): 100% deductible. Postage and the cost of shipping orders to customers are deductible business expenses.
- [Self-employment tax](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#self-employment-tax): 50% deductible. Half of your self-employment tax (the employer-equivalent part) is deductible in figuring adjusted gross income, on Schedule 1.
- [Business taxes](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#business-taxes): Partly deductible. Deductible: sales taxes imposed on you as the seller, real estate and personal property taxes on business assets, and federal highway use tax.
- [Business licenses and permits](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#licenses-permits): 100% deductible. Licenses and regulatory fees you pay each year to state or local governments for your business are deductible.
- [Commuting](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#commuting): Not deductible. Getting between your home and your regular place of work is commuting, a personal expense, however far it is and even if you work during the trip.
- [Fines and penalties](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#fines-penalties): Not deductible. Fines and penalties paid to a government for breaking a law aren't deductible, including traffic and parking tickets and tax penalties.
- [Political contributions and lobbying](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#political-lobbying): Not deductible. Contributions to candidates, campaigns and political parties aren't deductible, and neither are most costs of lobbying or trying to influence legislation or elections.
- [Club memberships](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#club-dues): Not deductible. Dues for clubs organized for business, pleasure, recreation or other social purposes, such as country clubs, golf and athletic clubs, airline and hotel clubs, aren't deductible.
- [Personal expenses](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#personal-expenses): Not deductible. Personal, living and family expenses aren't business deductions, even if paid from a business account.
- [Charitable donations by your business](https://mfa-advisory.com/tools/is-it-deductible/#charitable-contributions): Not deductible. A sole proprietor or single-member LLC can't deduct charitable contributions as a business expense on Schedule C.

- [Form 1065 for LLCs: Who Files, Due Date, K-1s, Step by Step](https://mfa-advisory.com/blog/form-1065-guide-llc/): Form 1065 for LLCs in plain English: which LLCs file it, the March 15, 2027 due date, K-1s for each member, the $260 late penalty and a step-by-step guide.
- [Adoption Tax Credit Refund 2026: IRS Sending Automatic Refunds](https://mfa-advisory.com/blog/adoption-tax-credit-refund-2026/): Adoption tax credit refund 2026: the IRS is sending automatic refunds to 50,000+ families with 2020-2024 carryforwards. No amended return needed. What to check.
- [AI in Accounting and Tax: What the IRS Says in 2026](https://mfa-advisory.com/blog/ai-in-accounting-and-tax-2026/): AI in accounting and tax: what the IRS's new 2026 AI guidelines say, where AI tools help with bookkeeping, and why you should verify any AI answer before you file.
- [SALT Cap 2026: The $40,400 Limit and the NJ and NY PTE Tax Fix](https://mfa-advisory.com/blog/salt-cap-2026-nj-ny-pte-tax/): SALT cap 2026: you can deduct up to $40,400 in state and local taxes, less above $505,000 of income. Year-end moves plus the NJ BAIT and NY PTET workaround.
- [ANCHOR Deadline 2026: NJ Property Tax Relief Is Due Nov. 2](https://mfa-advisory.com/blog/nj-property-tax-relief-anchor-stay-nj-2026/): The ANCHOR deadline for 2026 is Nov. 2. One PAS-1 form covers ANCHOR, Stay NJ (up to $6,500) and Senior Freeze. Who qualifies, amounts and who must file.
- [2027 Tax Calendar: Key IRS, New Jersey and New York Tax Deadlines](https://mfa-advisory.com/blog/2027-tax-calendar/): The 2027 tax calendar: every key IRS deadline plus New Jersey and New York due dates, from 1099s and W-2s to April 15 and estimated taxes. Save it to your calendar.
- [Year-End Tax Planning 2026: 4 Dates That Can Still Lower Your Tax Bill](https://mfa-advisory.com/blog/year-end-tax-planning-2026-key-dates/): Year-end tax planning 2026 in four dates: Oct. 15, Dec. 31, Jan. 15 and April 15. What to do by each one, with 2026 IRA, HSA and 401(k) limits.
- [Federal Scholarship Tax Credit 2027: The New $1,700 Credit Explained](https://mfa-advisory.com/blog/federal-scholarship-tax-credit-2027/): The federal scholarship tax credit starts Jan. 1, 2027: up to $1,700 per person for cash gifts to approved scholarship groups. Who qualifies, which states, and NJ.
- [Section 179 vs. Bonus Depreciation for 2026: Year-End Equipment Guide](https://mfa-advisory.com/blog/section-179-bonus-depreciation-2026/): Section 179 deduction 2026 limit is $2.56M and 100% bonus depreciation is back. How to write off equipment by Dec. 31, which to use, and the NJ catch.
- [Form 1099 Preparation Guide for 2026 Payments: The New $2,000 Rule and How to File Right](https://mfa-advisory.com/blog/form-1099-preparation-guide-2026/): The 1099-NEC and 1099-MISC threshold jumps to $2,000 for 2026 payments. Who needs a 1099, the 2027 deadlines, and a step-by-step QuickBooks process to file right.
- [October 15, 2026 Tax Extension Deadline: What to Do Before It Hits](https://mfa-advisory.com/blog/october-15-2026-tax-extension-deadline/): Filed an extension for your 2025 return? Your deadline is Thursday, Oct. 15, 2026. What to file, what waiting costs, and the NJ and disaster-area exceptions.
